policy.description: Blocking line-coverage ratchets. Update measured counts in the same reviewed change whenever scope or coverage advances; never lower a floor without an explicit, justified scope change.

tolerance.rationale: The #369 body-observer ownership fix adds one instrumented and covered client/core line so stale handles compare their exact subscriber identity before cleanup, advancing the reviewed high-water from 2326/2666 (87.247%) to 2327/2667 (87.252%). Two clean Node 22.20/V8 runs on 2026-07-27 each passed all 1788 tests across 233 files and reproduced exactly 2327/2667. Retaining the existing one-line tolerance makes the minimum 2326/2667 (87.214%), stricter than the prior 2325/2666 tolerated floor (87.209%). coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact below-floor, above-baseline, scope-change, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.

EP-01.4 (#507) adds the single Platform v1 pagination dialect: PlatformCursorCodec, PlatformPaging and PlatformPage, moving the instrumented scope from 36,489 to 36,569 lines. Every added line is exercised. PlatformPagingTests proves the two properties that matter - a full walk returns every row exactly once across six row-count/page-size combinations including the exactly-one-full-page case where an implementation is most likely to issue a cursor that returns nothing, and a cursor that is not ours is refused rather than silently restarting the walk, which would look like success to the client while producing duplicates. Refusal is covered for foreign-scope, other-server, tampered, malformed and truncated tokens. The ordering requirement is tested as a correctness requirement: a misordered source and a duplicate key are both refused, because without a total order 'everything after this key' is not a well-defined position. Opacity is asserted by checking the position does not appear in the token, and scope binding by proving the length-prefixed signature stops ('ab','c') and ('a','bc') from colliding. A guard test asserts no platform action exposes take/skip/page/size parameters, which is how three dialects grew on the legacy surface. Ten clean .NET 10.0.9/Coverlet runs on 2026-07-29 each passed all 2,442 tests at the same 36,569-line scope and measured 27,846 covered lines nine times and 27,847 once, so the reviewed high-water is 27,847 (76.147%). The observed spread was one line, but the tolerance is held at six rather than narrowed to match, because earlier scopes in this same repository showed spreads of five and six lines and CI hardware differs from the machine sampled here; narrowing to the luckiest observed window would convert ordinary Coverlet jitter into red builds. The floor still rises to 27,841/36,569 (76.130%) from the prior 27,763/36,489 (76.086%). An eleventh run was discarded rather than counted: it failed FileLoggerTests.ShutdownTimeout_ReturnsFalseWithoutBlockingCaller, a pre-existing wall-clock flake unrelated to this change, filed as #515. coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact scope-drift, regression, stale-baseline, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.
